Plot blocking indices

Source: R/fba-plot-blocking.R
plot_blocking.Rd

Draws the distribution of the participants' blocking indices as a violin with the individual values on top, and their mean with error bars of one standard error each way, in the style of Kelly and Ludvig (2025, Figure 3). The resulting figure stacks one panel per index above each other, with one violin per selection of test blocks.

Usage

plot_blocking(
  indices,
  index = c("bi_confidence", "bi_choice"),
  labels = NULL,
  parse = FALSE
)

Arguments

indices

Per-participant blocking indices, resulting from index_blocking(). Tables for several selections of blocks can be bound by rows first. For instance, the first block results can be combined with results based on all blocks.

index

Character. Indices to draw, by their column names in indices, i.e., any of "bi_confidence" and "bi_choice". Defaults to both.

labels

Named character, or NULL (default). Panel titles by index name, replacing the defaults ("Confidence-weighted choice score", "Choice-proportion score") for the indices named.

parse

Logical(1). Read labels as plotmath expressions? FALSE (default) prints them as they are. TRUE allows subscripts that do not depend on the font having subscript characters, e.g. c(bi_confidence = 'BI[2]*":"~"confidence-weighted choice score"').

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The dotted horizontal line marks zero, i.e., no blocking. The labels at the top and bottom of each panel name the outcome that the participants' answers lean towards. Selecting the Stage 3 outcome associated with the control cue yields positive values (i.e., blocking), while preference for the Stage 3 outcome associated with the putatively blocked cue yields negative ones. The vertical axis is symmetric around zero within each panel.

The function says that it ran aggregate_blocking() on your behalf and that function then states how its standard errors are defined. Run aggregate_blocking() yourself to get the numbers behind the figure.

References

Kelly, T., & Ludvig, E. A. (2025). Blocking of associative learning by explicit descriptions. Cognition, 256, 106015. doi:10.1016/j.cognition.2024.106015

See also

index_blocking(), aggregate_blocking()
